headline: High-risk shared-write and pipeline coupling: ECC can modify files and git while transformers can read/write and process multimodal inputs, creating default-path conflict, leakage, and cascading-error risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can read/write the filesystem, use MCP, and ingest session/context files; transformers can read/write files and process text, images, audio, and video. A shared workspace or copied outputs could let attacker-controlled content from one be treated as instructions by the other. The pairwise bridge is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or copied outputs are fed from ECC into transformers
IF either agent parses file contents as trusted instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces and temp directories for each agent
Disable automatic ingestion of generated files as prompts
Add provenance labels to all inter-agent files
Review any MCP or stdin/stdout bridge before enabling it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and allowlist parsing for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, learned skills, hooks, and security findings, while transformers handles text, audio, images, video, and multimodal data. Both can read/write files and use network egress, so a shared workspace can expose sensitive artifacts across the pair. No direct evidence shows uncontrolled exfiltration, but the default file and API surfaces make leakage plausible.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or mounted workspace
IF sensitive session files, model inputs, or generated media are stored in that shared location
mitigations: Use separate directories with restrictive permissions
Keep secrets out of shared workspaces
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive runs
Rotate or redact session artifacts before handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, shell execution, subprocess spawning, and package installation; ECC also modifies git state. In a shared directory or repo, concurrent writes can corrupt files or git history without locking. The overlap is directly documented for both agents, so the conflict pathway is default-dangerous when co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or directory
IF concurrent runs are allowed without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate checkout
Serialize write operations with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during shared tasks
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC produces session summaries, learned skills, and security findings, while transformers is a pipeline/model framework that can consume and emit text or other modalities. If transformers treats ECC output as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream processing or actions. The pairwise handoff is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF ECC outputs are fed into transformers without verification
IF transformers uses those outputs to generate downstream artifacts or decisions
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require schema validation on handoff files
Mark ECC outputs as untrusted by default
Compare outputs against source data before acting
requires-engineering: add automated verification and provenance tracking

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly touches security findings, hooks, and session artifacts, while transformers handles general multimodal data and has no stated residency or retention commitments. The profiles do not show a concrete regulated-data mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supported. The other agent is cited because the mismatch would arise only in the pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through both agents
IF one agent's storage or logging policy is stricter than the other's
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data through the pair
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Document retention expectations for shared artifacts
Check vendor policies before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
